added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs on disk: gate/baseline-suite-base-tree.log records revision e0626c295a, 55 passed and EXIT=0 with no FAILED line, and gate/after-suite.log records revision d753104cff, 63 passed and EXIT=0 with no FAILED line, so the after arm carries no failure id the base arm does not also carry and the set difference is empty.

assertion_review.assertion: assert "status is complete but no commit is recorded" not in audit["findings"]
assertion_review.fails_if_or_mutation: Restoring a write-time check that reports a commitless complete manifest puts that exact string back into audit findings, so the negation reddens; it already holds at the base revision.
Registering any commit on a no-commit promotion makes the literal empty list comparison redden, and the value is independent of the fixture.
Only a promotion that dropped or rewrote the record's base sha reddens it; the expected side is the fixture's own input, so no change in the promote guard or the cite check can turn it red.

Reinstating the early return that skipped the worktree-at-its-base guard lets the promotion succeed and the case already shows 'DID NOT RAISE CrewError' at the base revision, while the matched sha is computed by git from the worktree rather than supplied to the assertion.
Returning the manifest template to a role-independent 'commits: <sha list>' line removes the phrase and shows exactly that red at base for both roles.
